title: Catalog metadata playbook for onboarding open-vendor models and publishing performance profiles
creator: Priya Desai
description: Create a repeatable playbook and concrete metadata schema updates to onboard open-vendor models (community/open weights) into the Redwood model catalog. Include canonical fields for version pinning, compatibility matrix, quantization/variant mapping, and the process to publish canonical performance profiles and docs for customers and internal users.
background: Recent onboarding requests for community models exposed gaps in our catalog fields: missing runtime-compat flags, unclear variant lineage, and absence of standardized perf-profile attachments.
Goal: reduce manual friction and support predictable rollouts of new model variants with observable performance metrics and clear default pin recommendations.
work_items: Define additional metadata keys: runtime_compatibility, canonical_variant_id, recommended_pin, benchmark_suite_id, quantization_compatibility, kernel_profile_hint, caution_notes
Update model ingestion pipeline to accept the new keys and surface validation errors in CI linting
Author an internal onboarding playbook (Confluence) describing steps: ingest, run validation benchmarks, create performance profile, publish catalog entry, QA, and customer communication
Produce example catalog entries for two representative open-vendor models (one large decoder-only, one instruction-tuned chat model), including pinned version recommendations and fallback variants
Add automated step to register perf profile artifacts (benchmarks + raw traces) to the perf-dashboard and include link in catalog metadata
Coordinate with runtime team to include kernel_profile_hint that maps to kernel selection presets tested during onboarding
Update public docs page with a short 'What to expect' section for customers when a new open model lands in the catalog
Create a short migration guide for existing catalog entries that lack new fields (best-effort defaults and a 2-week window for owners to fill in).
updates: 2026-03-04: Kickoff meeting with product (Aisha Kapoor) and design (Evelyn Chen). Agreed scope: onboarding playbook + metadata schema changes + one example onboarding run.

2026-03-06: Draft metadata schema posted to docs repo: added runtime_compatibility (list of runtimes), canonical_variant_id, recommended_pin (string), benchmark_suite_id. Asked runtime team for review (marco@redwood).
2026-03-09: Runtime team (Liam O'Connor) proposed renaming 'kernel_profile_hint' to 'kernel_preset' and requested we include sequence_length_distribution sample. Accepted with small change.
2026-03-11: Engineering review: added quantization_compatibility field and a required 'minimal_supported_version' to indicate the earliest model version supported by our optimizations.
2026-03-12: Created draft onboarding playbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CATALOG/Open+Model+Onboarding+-+Playbook
2026-03-13: Ran initial benchmark for community-chat-v3 on a p4d cluster. Results attached to perf-dashboard and linked in PR: https://perf.redwood.ai/dashboards/bench-ENG-22456
2026-03-14: PM review (Aisha Kapoor) requested explicit rollback criteria and a customer comms template. Added to acceptance criteria.
design_feedback: Evelyn Chen: recommend a small UX addition to Console model page to show 'recommended_pin' with a one-click pin action for Dedicated customers.
Design asked for a concise human-friendly 'What changed' blurb in the public docs when a model is added or repinned.
engineering_notes: Validation: upstream lint will reject missing benchmark_suite_id for new catalog entries marked as 'public'.
Batching: documented expected throughput delta for quantized variants vs fp16 in perf-profile template.
Compatibility matrix: map of runtime tags -> supported feature flags will be encoded as comma-separated strings in runtime_compatibility field.
Pin strategy: recommended_pin should be semantic version or hash (we prefer semver-like tags for readability), and there will be a 'pin_expiry' cadence documented in playbook.
acceptance_criteria: New metadata schema published in docs repo and implemented in catalog ingestion service
Onboarding playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step checklist and rollback criteria
One example open-vendor model fully onboarded using the new process with public performance profile linked in the catalog entry
Console shows 'recommended_pin' in model detail page mock (Design sign-off obtained)
Benchmark artifacts visible on perf-dashboard and referenced in the catalog entry
Linting rule added to CI to require minimal_supported_version and benchmark_suite_id for public models
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: New fields could break older ingestion clients. Mitigation: ingestion service will default to legacy-behavior when fields are absent and emit a warning for owners.
Risk: Perf profiles for some community models may exhibit high variance. Mitigation: require 5 runs and a median/95th report and add 'variance_note' in profile metadata.
Risk: Customers may rely on a pinned variant that later regresses. Mitigation: add automatic regression alerting tied to eval prompts and link to rollout policy templates.

Complete the example onboarding run and publish perf artifacts to perf-dashboard (Liam)

PM to prepare customer comms template and decide pilot customer list (Aisha)
Schedule a cross-team review on 2026-03-18 to sign off on playbook and CI lint rule
notes: Keep public-facing documentation limited to high-level performance ranges and recommended pin; internal perf artifacts and raw traces remain behind our perf-dashboard permissioning.
